rv.q: I'll wager you won't regret going for a second, not with this much passion and creativity and sheer talent running around what long has been the most artistically satisfying basement in the city.
All in all, AMÉLIE is as charming and sweet as its protagonist.
With music direction by Anna Wegener and T.J. Anderson, “Amélie” is as buoyant and uplifting as a balloon bouquet.
This production is a diamond in a sea of late Summer theatrical offerings throughout the Chicagoland area.
“Amélie: The Musical” has it all from an outstanding, energetic cast to an accomplished technical team...
The result is a far more intimate and fanciful feel-good charmer that surpasses the original Broadway production.
Daniel Messeé’s whimsical score stirs up all the same kinds of emotions the movie does without oversimplifying the plot.
The preciousness of the film is eschewed for pure enchantment and loveliness.
Van Barham’s jolly production had me smiling long after the lights dimmed.
It’s a thoroughly joyful musical romp through Montmartre—garden gnome or no garden gnome.
Even with the brief blip, the ensemble’s sparkling performance kept me happily in orbit around Amélie’s strange, hopeful world.

Ultimately, Amélie The Musical provides a night of great music in a fun immersive set populated by a talented group of actors who double as musicians in a show seamlessly choreographed by director/choreographer Derek Van Barham and musical directors T.J.
The ensemble is sheer perfection, each and every one do their roles in a unique manner and brng the story to life with great artistry.
The production will leave you leaning full tilt into the light and opening your arms as you exit the theatre ready to embrace goodness awaiting you if you just let it in.
The opportunity to experience this unusual staging is worth the effort.

cn.t: Kokandy's intimate production transforms a Broadway flop into charming, whimsical delight, with critics praising its warmth and inventive staging while noting an aimless first act and occasional excess of quirk.
